title: Trace the auction when policy or features change
description: Choose a serving scenario to see which path is active, which component owns the decision, and why a useful fallback may reduce personalization without relaxing consent, budget, frequency, or delivery safeguards.

nodes.label: Ad opportunity
nodes.detail: Carries placement, deadline, region, approved contextual fields, and a consent reference. It never supplies permission by implication.

nodes.label: Auction gateway
nodes.detail: Validates request shape, attaches the trace and policy versions, limits fan-out, and sends only approved fields to downstream services.

nodes.label: Eligibility gate
nodes.detail: Checks consent, inventory, targeting rules, campaign status, frequency caps, and current budget authority before a candidate can be ranked.

nodes.label: Approved features
nodes.detail: Serves bounded contextual and consented first-party features with freshness and schema metadata. It is not an authority for consent or spending.

nodes.label: Ranker + pacing
nodes.detail: Scores a bounded eligible set, applies an explicit pacing multiplier, and can use an approved contextual-only model when personalization is unavailable.

nodes.label: Delivery guard
nodes.detail: Applies campaign-specific delivery and creative constraints, records the evaluated slice, and blocks rules that cannot be verified for the surface.

nodes.label: Auction + reservation
nodes.detail: Runs the documented pricing rule, atomically reserves spend for the selected eligible candidate, and returns one traceable decision before the deadline.

nodes.label: Decision event stream
nodes.detail: Records candidate set, positions, feature and policy versions, price, and later outcome events without delaying the auction response.

nodes.label: Evaluation + training
nodes.detail: Builds point-in-time training data and evaluates calibration, value, privacy, and delivery slices before a new model can be released.

scenarios.label: Healthy auction
scenarios.summary: All required authorities respond within the deadline. Eligible candidates are scored, delivery controls run, the winner reserves budget, and the decision is logged asynchronously.
scenarios.result: The response is fast because work is bounded, not because it skips constraints. The decision record makes later billing and evaluation explainable.

scenarios.label: Personalization outage
scenarios.summary: The approved personal-feature dependency is unavailable. The ranker uses its preapproved contextual-only feature subset, while all eligibility and delivery rules remain in force.
scenarios.result: Personalization and revenue may decline, but the system is explicit about the fallback and does not reuse expired or unconsented features.

scenarios.label: Consent cannot be verified
scenarios.summary: The gateway cannot obtain a required consent decision for the request. Candidate targeting that needs that signal never reaches ranking or the auction.
scenarios.result: Fail closed for the affected targeting path or use an independent, policy-approved contextual path. A timeout is not permission to profile or serve.

scenarios.label: Delivery fairness regression
scenarios.summary: Monitoring finds a material delivery disparity for a governed campaign slice. The guard blocks the affected configuration while evaluation retains versioned evidence for investigation.
scenarios.result: Do not hide a slice regression behind aggregate revenue. Pause or constrain the affected campaign configuration and roll back the responsible model or rule version.

scenarios.label: Budget reservation conflict
scenarios.summary: Several auctions try to spend the last budget amount at once. The auction cannot reserve the apparent winner, so it removes that candidate and continues before the deadline.
scenarios.result: The campaign may lose a marginal opportunity, but spend remains correct. Returning an unreserved winner would turn a concurrency conflict into overspend.
